newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac makes appeal in Lima hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Chirac makes appeal in Lima hostage crisis.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Thursday urged Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to deal humanely but firmly with the Lima hostage crisis in which leftist guerrillas are holding nearly 500 people hostage.

"This particularly tragic event threatens the lives of numerous Peruvian and foreign personalities and I do not doubt that your government will do all in its power to bring the situation under control with all the humanity and firmness required," Chirac wrote to the Peruvian leader.
Chirac said France condemned as unjustifiable the action in which the leftists took high-ranking diplomats, businessmen and government officials hostage at a Japanese embassy reception on Tuesday.
The rebels are threatening to kill the hostages unless 400 to 500 of their jailed comrades are released.
The rebels have released some hostages including French cultural attache Hyacinthe Montera.
Chirac wrote a separate letter to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto expressing sympathy and support in the face of what he called the rebels' "disgusting and cowardly attack".
